div.span: How to Trade Off the Dealer Hedging Simulator

div.p: This is a heuristic dealer-positioning read, not a signal generator — treat it as one input describing what kind of environment you're in (trending/breakout-prone vs. range-bound/pinned) and where the pressure points are, then combine it with your own entry/risk rules.
1. Regime first — decides your whole playbook.

ul.li: SHORT GAMMA — dealers must trade WITH price to stay hedged. Moves that start tend to continue; breakouts tend to run. Favor momentum/breakout entries, not fades.
LONG GAMMA — dealers trade AGAINST price. Expect chop/mean-reversion around the pin. Favor fading extremes, not chasing breakouts.
NEUTRAL — no edge here; wait, or lean on the addon's other tools (Bands, Zones, Signal Bot).

div.p: Check magnitude too, not just sign — Dealer Gamma barely past the dead zone is a weak read; deeply negative/positive is the conviction case.

2. Where is price relative to the Gamma Flip line? It's the boundary between the two regimes above. A clean break-and-hold through it is a genuine regime-change event — don't treat a brief wick through it as confirmation, wait for a close beyond it.

p.b: 3. Use Gamma Walls as levels, not direction.

ul.li: Green wall (dealer long gamma) = pin/support-resistance magnet. Good fade target in a long-gamma regime; a likely stalling point if you're riding a short-gamma move toward it.

Red wall (dealer short gamma) = acceleration level, not a magnet. Don't fade it in a short-gamma regime — a clean break tends to extend, not reverse. Poor place to chase a breakout in a long-gamma regime (more likely to snap back).

div.p: 4. Use the simulated forecast path as a directional lean, not a target. It only scales real recent momentum by the regime, so read its direction as confirmation, not its exact % as a take-profit. Best case: regime + flip position + forecast direction + wall layout all agree (confluence). If the forecast direction disagrees with the regime, trust the regime.

ul.li: Regime has real conviction (not neutral / not barely past the dead zone)
Price is clearly on one side of the Gamma Flip, not straddling it
Forecast box direction agrees with the regime-implied bias
No opposing wall sitting immediately in your path

div.p: Entry/stop sketch: short-gamma momentum trade — enter in the predicted direction, first target = nearest same-direction wall, stop beyond the Gamma Flip. Long-gamma fade trade — enter back toward the nearest wall/flip, stop beyond the wall you're fading. Re-check every refresh — dealer positioning shifts as new flow prints.

Expiry: Nearest (the default) — gamma scales roughly with 1/√T, so the nearest-dated contract dominates near-term hedging flow. Use Nearest+1 only as a secondary check. Avoid "All (cumulative)" for trade decisions — it blends distinct expiries' hedging dynamics together and is the heaviest, slowest read.

Window: All (full position) for your primary regime/wall read — a dealer's real exposure is accumulated, not daily-reset. Pair it with a 24h (or 8h) read as a secondary check: if they agree, that's added confidence; if they sharply disagree, fresh flow is actively repositioning the book and the signal is less reliable until it settles.
div.div: Caveats: dealers are assumed to be the counterparty to every trade — a simplification every public GEX tool makes, not verified counterparty data. The forecast path is a deterministic heuristic, not a price guarantee. Use alongside the rest of this addon (Bands, Zones, Signal Bot) and real risk management. This isn't financial advice.
